workflows.name: Team invite lifecycle
workflows.trigger: An admin invites a new member to the workspace by email.
steps: Enter invitee email and role
System sends invite email with a token link
Invitee accepts and creates/links their account
Invitation is marked accepted

workflows.name: API key lifecycle
workflows.trigger: A developer creates an API key to integrate with the product.
steps: Create a key with a name and scopes
Key is shown once and stored hashed
Key is used for authenticated API calls
Key is revoked or naturally expires

workflows.name: Webhook delivery
workflows.trigger: A subscribed event occurs and must be delivered to the workspace's webhook endpoint.
steps: Event occurs and is queued for delivery
Worker POSTs the signed payload
Endpoint responds 2xx (success) or non-2xx (retry)
Retries exhaust or succeed

workflows.name: SSO connection setup
workflows.trigger: A workspace admin configures SAML SSO against their identity provider.
steps: Admin enters IdP metadata URL or XML
System verifies the metadata and stores the connection
Admin tests a login
Connection goes live for the workspace

workflows.name: Data export request
workflows.trigger: A workspace owner requests an export of their tenant's data.
steps: Owner requests an export
Job is queued and processed asynchronously
A download link is generated and emailed
Link expires after a retention window

workflows.name: Workspace offboarding
workflows.trigger: A workspace owner deletes their workspace, with an export offer and a grace period before hard deletion.
steps: Owner requests deletion
System offers a data export
Workspace enters a grace period
Workspace is hard-deleted after the grace period, or deletion is cancelled

workflows.name: Status incident lifecycle
workflows.trigger: Platform support publishes and updates a status-page incident during an outage.
steps: Open an incident and set severity
Post updates as the cause is identified
Post a fix-deployed update
Resolve the incident

workflows.name: Sign-up to onboarded workspace
workflows.trigger: A new user signs up and creates their first workspace.
steps: User creates an account and a new workspace
Workspace starts on a trial or free plan
Owner is guided through a first-run onboarding checklist (branding, first invite, key integration)
Checklist completion is tracked; owner can skip and resume later

provenance.notes: Both Chatwoot's onboarding controller/service and Twenty CRM's onboarding modules implement signup-to-first-workspace guided setup.

workflows.name: Usage metering to quota enforcement
workflows.trigger: A usage event is recorded against a workspace's metered entitlement.
steps: System records a usage event (API call, seat-day, storage, etc.)
Usage is aggregated and compared against the workspace's plan entitlement limit
A quota-warning notification is sent as usage approaches the limit
At the limit, the system applies overage billing or throttles further usage per plan policy

provenance.notes: Lago's UsageThreshold model and OpenMeter's featuremeter module both implement usage-vs-limit evaluation driving warnings/overage.

workflows.name: Plan upgrade or downgrade with proration
workflows.trigger: A workspace owner changes their subscription's plan tier from the billing portal.
steps: Owner selects a new plan tier
System computes a prorated charge or credit for the remainder of the billing period
Owner confirms the change and, on upgrade, the payment method is charged
New entitlements and seat limits apply immediately; downgrades that exceed the new limits are flagged for resolution

provenance.notes: boxyhq's Stripe-backed Subscription/Price models and Lago's Plan/Wallet models both support changing a subscription's plan; proration is standard behavior of the Stripe Billing/Lago APIs they integrate.

workflows.name: Failed payment to dunning to suspension
workflows.trigger: A recurring subscription charge fails.
steps: Payment provider reports a failed charge; workspace subscription moves to past_due
System retries the charge on a backoff schedule and sends dunning emails to the owner
If payment is recovered, the workspace returns to active
If retries are exhausted, the workspace is suspended pending payment

provenance.notes: boxyhq's Stripe webhook handler enumerates past_due/canceled subscription statuses, confirming the billing-provider-level states, but no dedicated dunning-email sequence or suspension logic was found in the repo; the retry/dunning/suspension sequence itself is a reasoned inference from standard Stripe Billing/Lago dunning behavior, stated explicitly as low confidence.

workflows.name: Trial start to conversion or expiry
workflows.trigger: A workspace starts a time-boxed trial of a paid plan.
steps: Workspace enters trial with the trial plan's full entitlements for a fixed number of days
System sends a reminder before the trial ends
Owner adds a payment method and converts to a paid plan, or takes no action
On expiry without conversion, the workspace downgrades to a restricted/free tier; late conversion remains possible

provenance.notes: boxyhq's Stripe integration exposes the 'trialing' status; Twenty CRM implements the full flow (billing-trial-ending/-converting emails, billing-trial-period/-end-trial-period DTOs, UpgradeFreeTrial page).

workflows.name: Seat reservation to reclaim
workflows.trigger: A workspace admin invites or removes a member, changing seat usage against the plan.
steps: Admin invites a member; a seat is reserved (pending) against the plan's seat entitlement
Invite is accepted; the seat becomes active
Inviting past the seat limit is blocked or prompts a plan/seat upgrade
Admin removes a member; their seat is reclaimed and available for reuse

provenance.notes: boxyhq ties TeamMember to a per-team Subscription; Lago models subscription quantity/wallet balances that map to seat-style consumption and reclaim.

workflows.name: SCIM provisioning to deprovisioning
workflows.trigger: The customer's identity provider pushes a SCIM user or group event.
steps: Admin enables SCIM and generates a bearer token for the workspace
The token and SCIM base URL are configured in the customer's IdP
IdP pushes user create/update/deactivate events via SCIM
System provisions, updates, or deactivates the corresponding workspace member

provenance.notes: Implementation (boxyhq's Jackson dsync + SCIM v2.0 routes) plus the authoritative SCIM RFCs.

workflows.name: Feature flag gradual rollout
workflows.trigger: A new feature is gated behind a flag for gradual release.
steps: Flag is created disabled by default
Flag is targeted at specific workspaces or segments for early access
Rollout percentage is gradually increased
Flag is fully enabled for all workspaces, or rolled back on issues

provenance.notes: Both Unleash (strategies/constraints) and Flagsmith (FeatureState/FeatureSegment) implement staged/segmented rollout.

workflows.name: Audit log review
workflows.trigger: An admin needs to review who changed what in the workspace.
steps: Admin opens the audit log viewer and filters by date range, actor, or action type
Admin inspects an entry's detail (actor, target, before/after, timestamp)
Admin exports the filtered results for compliance or investigation purposes

provenance.notes: boxyhq's Retraced integration and Chatwoot's dashboard audit-log viewer both implement filter/inspect/export over a tenant-scoped audit log.

workflows.name: Support impersonation session
workflows.trigger: Support staff need to reproduce or resolve an issue from inside a tenant's workspace.
steps: Support searches for and opens the tenant's workspace in the admin console
Support starts an impersonation session, shown to any observer via a visible impersonation banner
Support takes the necessary action as if signed in as the tenant user; the session is written to the audit log
Support ends the impersonation session, returning to their own staff account

provenance.notes: Chatwoot's ImpersonationBanner.vue + useImpersonation.js implement a real, visible impersonation session; SOC 2's CC6/CC7 access-control criteria motivate auditing such sessions.

workflows.name: Changelog entry publishing
workflows.trigger: A change ships and is announced to workspace members.
steps: Entry is drafted and categorized (feature, fix, improvement)
Entry is published to the public/in-app changelog feed
Members see an unread-updates indicator until they view the feed

provenance.notes: Chatwoot's changelog feed with an unread-indicator sidebar button, and Twenty CRM's structured release-notes page, both implement draft-then-publish changelog entries.

workflows.name: Custom role authoring
workflows.trigger: A workspace owner needs finer-grained permissions than the built-in owner/admin/member roles.
steps: Owner creates a new role with a name
Owner selects permission grants from the available scopes (per-object, per-field, or row-level where supported)
Owner assigns the role to one or more members
Permission changes apply immediately to all members holding the role

provenance.notes: Chatwoot's customRole.js and Twenty CRM's object/field/row-level role-permission authoring UI both implement this create-role-then-assign flow.

workflows.name: Per-key API rate limit enforcement
workflows.trigger: A request against the public API arrives authenticated by an API key.
steps: System looks up the rate limit for the key's workspace/plan
Current usage in the window is checked against the limit
Within limit: request proceeds and rate-limit headers are returned
Over limit: request is rejected with a 429 response

provenance.notes: Chatwoot's rack_attack throttles by account_id/API token; Twenty CRM's throttler module explicitly builds standard rate-limit response headers (build-rate-limit-response-headers.util.ts).

workflows.name: Sandbox environment provisioning
workflows.trigger: A developer needs to integration-test without touching production tenant data.
steps: Developer enables sandbox mode for the workspace, or a separate sandbox workspace is created
System provisions an isolated environment seeded with synthetic data
Developer tests against the sandbox using a sandbox-scoped API key
Sandbox data is periodically reset or expires

provenance.notes: No sandbox-workspace implementation was found in any source checked this pass (boxyhq, Chatwoot, Twenty CRM); this workflow describes the standard test/live-mode pattern common to API-first SaaS (as in payment-provider test modes), anchored only to the API-key entity boxyhq does implement. Confidence deliberately low, matching the feature's own low confidence.

workflows.name: Data residency region selection
workflows.trigger: An enterprise workspace must pin where its data is stored and processed.
steps: Owner selects a data region during workspace creation or later in settings
System validates the region is supported and available
Data storage/processing is confirmed pinned to that region
Changing region later requires a data migration process

provenance.notes: Twenty CRM's DATA_RESIDENCY_KEYS config and settings UI implement region selection (for its AI feature); GDPR cross-border transfer rules are the authoritative motivation for offering the control at all.
